key: folk:crocodile:The Cinder Drake|dragon|dragon|rust|Late Cretaceous, 66 million years ago|

narrator.persona: a calm, warm storyteller, like a nature documentary narrator who is quietly afraid

sentences.text: For millions of years the sky belonged to the flying reptiles and the ground to the Tyrannosaurus rex, and nothing had ever challenged either.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: Countless winged predators drifted through the red sunset, knowing no fear from anything above.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: Then a dead volcano woke beneath the valley, making the ground shudder and the horizon bleed.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: The mountain burst open as black smoke choked the sun, sending herds and the great king fleeing together.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: Deep inside the burning crater something massive shifted, forged from jagged horns, obsidian scales, and living fire.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: It snapped its vast wings and rose, instantly scattering the ancient flyers who suddenly realized they were prey.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: The old king roared a futile challenge upward, but the beast answered with a blinding flash of white heat.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: The sky and the ground now belonged to a single tyrant, leaving us to wonder what else sleeps beneath the ash.
sentences.speaker: narrator
